analysis.title: Middle East Weekly Tracker: Oil flows through Hormuz fall as tanker attacks continue
key_insights: US-Iran talks remain stalled despite mediation by Oman and Qatar. Iran launched its third attack in five days on US military targets in Bahrain on 17 November.
Bahrain said the drones were intercepted. The US military reported no injuries or damage to its equipment. The US responded by striking an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island.
In Yemen, Saudi-backed government forces withdrew from the Bab el-Mandeb area on 15 November to defend Aden as the Houthis gained ground along the southern coast.
Brent fell to USD92/bbl on 18 November. The IEA forecasts global oil supply exceeding demand by 1.7 million barrels a day in Q4, while fresh tanker incidents highlight risks to Middle East exports.
GCC 5-year CDS spreads remained relatively stable through the week.
Abu Dhabi led Gulf equity markets in the week to 17 November, helped by First Abu Dhabi Bank's rally after it announced plans to raise capital.
Foreign investors bought a net USD151mn of Saudi and Dubai equities in the week to 15 November, down from USD219mn the previous week.

Ship-to-ship transfers and alternative routes lifted Gulf oil flows to more than 70% of pre-war levels in October. Renewed Iranian tanker attacks have disrupted that recovery, with estimated crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz declining since late October.
The UKMTO recorded seven tanker attacks in the week ending 11 November.
